To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of excess of oxalate in the solution enhances the photocatalytic reduction rate of Cr(VI) over UV-irratiated TiO2 and that this effect is related to the presence of Cr(V) complexes.
the presence of oxalic acid facilitates the photocatalytic reduction process, but the reduction mechanism does not follow the electron shuttle mechanism.
the photocatalytic reduction over TiO2 of Cr(VI) in the presence of an excess of oxalate is mainly due to a sequential electron-transfer process involving Cr(V) intermediates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the photocatalytic reduction mechanism of Cr(VI) in the presence of TiO2 particles and oxalate.
the identification of the key intermediates in Cr(VI)-reduction processes and the understanding of the reaction mechanisms involved.
the elucidation of the photocatalytic reduction mechanisms of Cr(VI) in aqueous solution over TiO2 in the presence of different ligands and under different pH conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cr(V) oxalato complexes are not the main intermediates of the Cr(VI)-photocatalyzed reduction process.

the photocatalytic reduction over TiO2 of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) is a complex process, in which the reduction of the Cr(VI)/Cr(V)/Cr(III) system takes place through sequential one-electron transfer steps, with the formation of Cr(V) oxalato complexes as key intermediates.
the Cr(VI)/oxalate photocatalytic reaction is a complex process in which several mechanisms take place simultaneously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photocatalytic reduction mechanism for Cr(VI), in the presence of organic ligands, is similar to the one in the absence of them, but the rate constants are significantly different.
Cr(VI) can be effectively photocatalytically reduced in the presence of electron shuttles such as oxalate, EDTA, or citrate, but the electron-shuttle effect is more important at pH 3 than at pH 2.
the photocatalytic reduction mechanism of Cr(VI) over irradiated TiO2 is not affected by the nature of the ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of oxalic acid in the reaction medium does not prevent the formation of chromium(V) species during Cr(VI) photoreduction.
Cr(V) oxalato species, formed during the photocatalytic reduction process, are unstable and undergo a fast photodegradation.
Cr(VI) can be reduced to Cr(III) by TiO2 photocatalysis in the presence of an excess of oxalate.
